items.title: SIR did not affect electoral results; ECI opposes TMC plea for fresh polls in 31 West Bengal seats
items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has told the Supreme Court that 37,05,235 appeals arising out of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal are pending before the Appellate Tribunals. Out of the only 1,26,194 appeals have been decided so far. The disclosure came in the ECI's reply to an application by Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O'Brien. Pertinently, the ECI opposed O'Brien's plea for fresh polls in 31 West Bengal assembly seats. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana had earlier directed the ECI to specify how many appeals were presently pending before election tribunals. According to the data furnished by ECI: - Total appeals filed: 38,31,429 - Filed by voters whose names were excluded or deleted: 22,21,118 - Appeals against inclusion: 16,10,311 - Decided: 1,26,194 - Pending: 37,05,235 Murshidabad and Malda account for the most appeals, with 7,48,216 and 5,31,617 respectively. Murshidabad has decided 595 of its appeals. The only other records of Demoiselle Crane sighting from Tamil Nadu comes from Vijayanarayanam Tank in Tirunelveli. Naman Bora and Amoggh Chatty found the vagrant bird feeding in the reeds at Nemmeli salt pans near Chennai; the former would return to the spot the next three days and find the bird tenaciously clinging to this feeding spot
